messages:
incident-bot: ⚠️ PG: Dedicated pool eu-west-1 reporting p99 generation latency > 5s (SLO p99=2s). Affected route: /v1/generate (streaming). Alerts: grafana:red, logs:inference-queue-error. Root ts: 1791111111

oncall-sre-jules: I see it. p95 ~ 900ms, p99 ~ 5.3s, streaming stalls observed. Queue depth jumped from 20 -> 480 over 2m. Screenshots on the grafana link: https://grafana.redwood/eu-west1/dashboard/latency?orgId=1

eng-runtime-maya: digging into runtime logs now. Early suspicion: warmup of new replicas is taking ~140s due to KV-cache coldpath and quantized kernel alignment. Warmup failures show repeated model-load retries and long gc pauses.

eng-platform-lee: autoscaler events around same time show delayed handshake with pool controller; scale delta requested +12 but only +3 pods provisioned in 3m. Underlying cloud reports instance boot pending due to capacity constraints in the zone.

prod-support-sam: Customer CS tickets trickling in. One high-volume customer (acct: vimeo-app) reporting streaming stalls and partial responses. CS flagged potential data-loss concerns.

oncall-sre-jules: Triage actions: 1) stop accepting new long-lived streams on dedicated pool, 2) enable overflow routing to hosted api for non-sensitive tenants, 3) manual scale up of dedicated pool if capacity available, 4) gather heap/kvcache metrics and stack traces.

eng-runtime-maya: quick commands I ran:
```
# check pod readiness and restart counts
kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=eu-west1-dedicated -o wide
kubectl -n inference describe pod <hot-pod-id>
# view model load logs (tail)
kubectl -n inference logs <hot-pod-id> --since=10m | grep -i "model load" -A5
```
Logs show repeated "failed to mmap weights: EBUSY" and subsequent fallback to CPU path causing 10x slower token generation.

eng-platform-lee: cloud side: capacity shortage in eu-west-1c delaying instance allocation. I can 1) switch pool to other AZs, 2) request burst instances (costly), or 3) enable hosted overflow. Which do we want?

oncall-sre-jules: Prioritize lowest customer impact: enable hosted overflow for non-enterprise tenants now. For enterprise customers (vimeo-app), open an emergency cutover to alternate eu region if they allow cross-region.

cs-anna: Vimeo-app says cross-region is allowed for non-PII workloads. They want a heads-up before reroute. I'll ping their on-call.

prod-support-sam: Applied temporary rate limit for vimeo-app to reduce queue depth and avoid partial outputs. Sending customer DM: "We're throttling requests temporarily while we mitigate — aim to keep your SLA intact."

eng-runtime-maya: I pushed a config to reduce streaming concurrency per-connection to 2 (was 8) on the dedicated pool. Command:
```
# lower concurrency via config map
kubectl -n inference patch configmap pool-eu-west1-dedicated -p '{"data":{"streaming.max_concurrency":"2"}}'
# trigger rolling config rollout
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/inference-pool-eu-west1-dedicated
```
This should reduce tail queuing pressure but will reduce throughput.

eng-platform-lee: Manual scale performed: requested +10 nodes in pool, cloud accepted +6 (now total nodes +6). New pods are starting but warmup still ~90-150s per replica. We need faster warmup or pre-warmed hotshots for burst traffic.

ops-ryan: Oncall note: warmup time is primarily model load + KV cache populate. We can accelerate by preloading KV heatmap from snapshot — I can trigger a k8s job to seed cache on startup. Two options: 1) safe quickseed (partial), 2) full-seed (longer). Recommend quickseed now.

eng-runtime-maya: Quickseed job ready. Command:
```
kubectl -n inference apply -f jobs/kv-cache-quickseed.yaml
# job will target new pods with label warmup=quickseed
```
Starting quickseed; monitoring latency.

incident-bot: NOTE: pg: page escalated to SEV2; paging oncall handoff in 30m. Use #incidents for updates.

oncall-sre-jules: Oncall handoff plan: @eng-runtime-maya will stay the lead for 30m, then handoff to @eng-platform-lee for follow-up (capacity/infra). @prod-support-sam to coordinate customer comms. If p99 remains >3s after 20m, escalate to the duty manager.

eng-runtime-maya: After quickseed started, p99 dropped to ~2.6s from 5.3s over 7m. Streaming stalls reduced but not gone. There's still a tail of clients with long KV fetch times.

eng-platform-lee: For longer-term: we should add a pre-warmed hotshot pool of tiny-instances (preloaded weights) for burst handling and also tune autoscaler to request instances earlier (lower threshold). I'll open a follow-up RFC but will implement an emergency autoscale-sensitivity bump now.

prod-support-sam: CS update: Vimeo-app acknowledged throttling, reporting fewer dropped responses. They've accepted cross-region fallback subject to a short maintenance window. Good enough for now.

ops-ryan: I'm running an evict-probe to move some non-critical pods off the overloaded AZ to free placement slots. Command: `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data <node-id>` (careful). Doing one node at a time.

oncall-sre-jules: Current status (T+18m): p95=850ms, p99=2.6s, queue depth=120, streaming stalls reduced by ~70%. Hosted overflow active for non-enterprise tenants. Manual scale increased pool by +6 nodes. Quickseed helped warmup.

eng-runtime-maya: Remaining action items before handoff: 1) confirm all new pods completed quickseed, 2) verify no "EBUSY" mmap events in last 10m, 3) run synthetic streaming load to validate tail. I'll run load test in 5m and post results.

prod-support-sam: Noting customer impact: 4 customers reported partial stalls, 1 enterprise (vimeo-app) saw degraded quality for ~9m. We should prepare incident summary for CS and billing.

oncall-sre-jules: Handoff to @eng-platform-lee in 12m. If any regression, re-page. Posting final mitigation summary here when I hand off.

eng-platform-lee: Ack handoff. I'll follow up with cloud to request temporary capacity reservation for eu-west-1c and open a postmortem to tune warmup and autoscaler thresholds. Also will add an emergency runbook entry: "when warmup >90s -> enable quickseed + hosted overflow".

incident-bot: RESOLVE CHECK: If stable for 30m, status -> mitigated and page closed.

oncall-sre-jules: Marking mitigations active. Leaving notes for next oncall: verify fullseed for long-term nodes during a low-traffic window, and scope pre-warm hotshot pool.
